Now it’s time for the final touches. Designed to reduce the risk of collisions with elk, deer and other wildlife, this project is scheduled to be completed later this year. ▪️State Route 87 Improvement Project in Payson: Following a winter pause, initial work will focus on sidewalk, driveway and crosswalk ramps. Pavement resurfacing along five miles of SR 87 between Green Valley Parkway and Crackjack Road is expected to begin by May. ▪️State Route 89A in Oak Creek Canyon: Work will start in April to replace old guardrail along the SR 89A switchbacks on the north end of Oak Creek Canyon (approximately 13 miles north of Sedona). ▪️I-40 Pavement improvements: Work has resumed on a resurfacing project between Holy Moses Wash and Rattlesnake Wash (mileposts 47-58) in Kingman. Work also will resume in April on a resurfacing project between Two Guns (milepost 230) and Meteor City Road (mileposts 230-240) west of Winslow. And a new project will replace the worn pavement from US 93 east to Silver Springs Road (mileposts 72-80). ▪️State Route 64 Improvement Project in Williams: Starting in April, this project will resurface 19 miles of SR 64 between the I-40 interchange and Pipeline Road, along with other improvements. ▪️US 160 Pavement Preservation: Work on a 14 mile stretch of US 160 both in and east of Tuba City (mileposts 321-335) is starting in April. Drivers should expect lane closures and traffic shifts while work takes place Mondays through Thursdays. Completion is scheduled by this fall. Use caution in work zones and plan for restrictions while this work is underway.Arizona Department of Transportation22.4K views · 21h ago0:28Wait…WHAT?! They’re already placing concrete pavment in Tucson in the median of the I-10 Kino to Country Club project?! 🤯 Yep — crews have already started placing Portland Cement Concrete Pavement (PCCP) in the median where traffic will switch to later this year. Here’s what’s happening step by step 👇 Step one - Setting the Reinforcement Workers place dowel bar baskets on the base layer to ensure proper load transfer across pavement joints. Step two - Delivering the Concrete Ready-mix trucks dump fresh concrete in front of the GOMACO slipform paver, where an auger spreads it evenly. Step three - Shaping the Pavement The slipform paver extrudes the concrete to the exact width, thickness, crown, and cross-slope—while vibrating and smoothing it into a uniform surface. Step four - Finishing the Surface Crews follow behind using floats and finishing tools to remove imperfections and prepare the pavement for tining. Step five - Tining for Safety Tiny parallel grooves are added to the surface to reduce skidding in wet conditions and improve traction for braking and steering.Arizona Department of Transportation135.6K views · 1d ago0:12The I-10 bridges over the Gila River are being widened and will have three travel lanes in each direction instead of two.
